findings.title: sunrise: potential oracle-manipulation entry point (score 5)
findings.description: [RECON HYPOTHESIS — specialist confirmation required] sunrise (user, external payable) in contracts/beanstalk/sun/SeasonFacet/SeasonFacet.sol. moves_funds=True, reads_external_state=True, modifiers=['fundsSafu', 'noOutFlow']. Intent: Manipulate the BEAN price oracle in the same block that sunrise() reads it, so deltaB is wrong and Beanstalk mints/burns the wrong supply, profiting the caller via mispriced soil/pods/rewards. Technique: Permissionless call to sunrise()->gm() at SeasonFacet.sol#37/48; gm() calls stepOracle() (deltaB) then stepSun() (Sun.sol#41) which mints Beans (C.bean().mint at Sun.sol#46) and sets soil/pod issuance; an attacker who skews the Well/pump reserves immediately before the season boundary biases deltaB and the freshly-minted supply distribution. Evasion: Beanstalk relies on TWA pump reserves rather than spot price to resist single-block manipulation; gap is whether the TWA window and the once-per-season cadence fully neutralise a multi-block or first-after-gap manipulation — oracle specialist must confirm the pump freshness/window.
findings.impact: Potential attacker entry point — requires specialist confirmation
findings.recommendation: Specialist review required. See ITE decomposition in attack_surface.json.

findings.title: gm: potential oracle-manipulation entry point (score 5)
findings.description: [RECON HYPOTHESIS — specialist confirmation required] gm (user, public payable) in contracts/beanstalk/sun/SeasonFacet/SeasonFacet.sol. moves_funds=True, reads_external_state=True, modifiers=['fundsSafu', 'noOutFlow']. Intent: Same as sunrise() but with attacker-chosen reward recipient — drive season advancement on manipulated oracle state to mint Beans and set soil/pod issuance in attacker's favour. Technique: gm(account,mode) at SeasonFacet.sol#48 runs stepOracle()->stepSun()->incentivize(); the whole season step (germination, gauge, sun minting) executes off one oracle read of deltaB. Caller controls timing relative to mempool/Well state. Evasion: require(seasonTime()>current) limits to one call per season; reward is the only direct payout. The economic risk is the indirect mint/soil sizing, not the incentive — needs economic_attack + oracle confirmation of TWA robustness.

findings.title: claimFertilized: potential reentrancy entry point (score 4)
findings.description: [RECON HYPOTHESIS — specialist confirmation required] claimFertilized (user, external payable) in contracts/beanstalk/barn/FertilizerFacet.sol. moves_funds=True, reads_external_state=False, modifiers=['fundsSafu', 'noSupplyChange', 'oneOutFlow']. Intent: Re-enter Beanstalk through the Fertilizer ERC-1155 update/payFertilizer callback path to over-claim rinsable Beans (Sprouts). Technique: claimFertilized() (FertilizerFacet.sol#47) calls C.fertilizer().beanstalkUpdate(...) which (Fertilizer._update at Fertilizer.sol#77) calls back into the diamond via IBS(owner()).payFertilizer(); fertilizedPaidIndex is updated at L52 and Beans sent at L53. The cross-contract callback (Beanstalk->Fertilizer->Beanstalk) is the reentrancy seam. Evasion: No nonReentrant on claimFertilized (only oneOutFlow); the Fertilizer side methods are onlyOwner so only the diamond can invoke them, but the payFertilizer re-entry into the diamond mid-update is the gap. reentrancy specialist to trace the diamond<->Fertilizer round trip.

findings.title: fillPodOrder: potential reentrancy entry point (score 4)
findings.description: [RECON HYPOTHESIS — specialist confirmation required] fillPodOrder (user, external payable) in contracts/beanstalk/market/MarketplaceFacet/MarketplaceFacet.sol. moves_funds=True, reads_external_state=False, modifiers=['fundsSafu', 'noSupplyChange', 'oneOutFlow']. Intent: Re-enter the marketplace during the Bean payout to a filler to refill/cancel the same order twice, extracting Beans escrowed in podOrders beyond what the order funded. Technique: fillPodOrder()->_fillPodOrder() (Order.sol#79): order balance is decremented at L105 then LibTransfer.sendToken(C.bean(),costInBeans,filler,mode) at L107, THEN _transferPlot at L113 and delete at L115-117. The plot transfer and order deletion happen AFTER the outbound token send; with To.INTERNAL or a Bean-side hook the post-send state is reachable. Evasion: oneOutFlow(C.BEAN) invariant bounds net Bean outflow, and order amount is debited before the send (partial CEI). No nonReentrant on this entry (unlike transferPlot). reentrancy specialist must confirm whether oneOutFlow fully blocks a second fill within the same tx.

findings.title: transferToken: potential access-control entry point (score 4)
findings.description: [RECON HYPOTHESIS — specialist confirmation required] transferToken (internal, internal nonpayable) in contracts/beanstalk/migration/L1Libraries/LibTransfer.sol. moves_funds=True, reads_external_state=False, modifiers=['(none)']. Intent: If any facet ever calls LibTransfer.transferToken with an attacker-controllable 'sender', an attacker could move tokens out of an arbitrary holder who has approved Beanstalk (arbitrary safeTransferFrom). Technique: transferToken()->safeTransferFrom(sender,recipient,amount) at LibTransfer.sol#42 uses the caller-supplied 'sender' as the from address (slither arbitrary-send-erc20, High). Exploitable only if a public entry passes a user-controlled sender rather than LibTractor._user(). Evasion: All audited call sites (MarketplaceFacet.fillPodListing, etc.) pass LibTractor._user() as sender, so the from address is authenticated. Gap: any new/forgotten caller that forwards a raw address param. access_control + token_integration to grep all callers for a non-_user() sender.

findings.title: claimPlenty: potential reentrancy entry point (score 4)
findings.description: [RECON HYPOTHESIS — specialist confirmation required] claimPlenty (user, external payable) in contracts/beanstalk/silo/SiloFacet/ClaimFacet.sol. moves_funds=True, reads_external_state=False, modifiers=['fundsSafu', 'noSupplyChange', 'oneOutFlow', 'nonReentrant']. Intent: Re-enter Beanstalk during the SOP token payout to double-claim Flood plenty, draining the protocol's plentyPerSopToken balance for a non-Bean (possibly hook-bearing) well token. Technique: claimPlenty()->_claimPlenty() (ClaimFacet.sol#95): LibTransfer.sendToken(sopToken,...) at L100 transfers the SOP token to the user BEFORE s.accts[account].sop.perWellPlenty[well].plenty is zeroed at L101 and plentyPerSopToken decremented at L104 — a CEI violation. If sopToken or its To.INTERNAL path yields control, the stale non-zero plenty can be re-read. Evasion: nonReentrant on the external claimPlenty()/claimAllPlenty() blocks classic same-facet reentrancy; gaps are (a) read-only/cross-function reentrancy if another facet reads perWellPlenty mid-flow, and (b) reliance on the SOP well token being a plain ERC-20 with no transfer hook. reentrancy specialist to confirm guard scope and token type.
